newsitem.title: FRANCE: Eramet shares rise as board meets.
newsitem.headline: Eramet shares rise as board meets.

text.p: Shares in nickel producer Eramet rose on Wednesday amid speculation a board meeting would provide fresh news on a long-standing dispute over the distribution of mining assets in New Caledonia, dealers and analysts said.
Eramet was up 1.75 percent to 290 francs at 0835 GMT, outpacing the blue-chip CAC-40 index which was up 1.28 percent.
The board meeting started around 0800 GMT, company officials said.

The board meeting had been delayed from June 24 to give the new Socialist government more time to review issues linked to a bitter row between Eramet and the previous conservative government over mining rights in New Caledonia,
Main shareholder state-holding Erap had threatened to take control of the board and oust chairman Yves Rambaud who opposes any plans to curb the group's expansion in New Caledonia.

The previous government supported a plan by local Kanak company Societe Miniere de Sud Pacifique (SMSP) to build a rival nickel smelter in the north of the French territory with Canadian group Falconbridge using nickel from one of Eramet's mines.
The move was to appease local Kanak separatists ahead of a 1998 referedum on independence.
The new Socialist government has not yet disclosed its plans on this highly politically sensitive issue but analysts said they expected the new administration to adopt a less confrontational line.
"It cannot be worse than it was," one analyst said, adding he expected Rambaud would stay on.
"The main unknown is the position of the French government. I do not expect a final solution today but they may provide some clues", he added.
Board members are expected to set a date for the annual shareholders' meeting.
Beside Erap's proposal to oust Rambaud board members were to have reviewed on June 24 proposals by minority shareholders aimed at insuring the independence of the board.
